prompt: Scan of a damaged black-and-white family photograph from the 1950s: a family of four in front of a suburban house next to a parked car, parents standing, two children in front, everyone smiling at the camera. The print is faded and low-contrast, with two deep creases crossing the image, a torn-off bottom-left corner, a brown water stain top-right, scattered dust and scratches, and a scalloped white paper border. Slightly skewed on the scanner. 5:4 landscape. No text.

Restore the attached old photograph in two layers of work.

Repair: remove the creases, tears, water stain and dust; rebuild the missing corner using the surrounding content; recover contrast and detail in the faded areas. Keep every face, pose, garment and background object exactly as in the original; do not reinterpret expressions or add anything that was not there.

Colourise: period-plausible, restrained colours for the 1950s: muted fabric tones, natural skin, a soft blue sky, no oversaturation. Keep the light grain of the original so it still reads as a photograph of its time, not a modern render.

Output the photo alone, straightened, without the paper border.
